contradictions: The two 0x500/0x2D0 sets differ in full r7 (0x28280106 versus 0x1A200136) and in low-six-bit value (0x06 versus 0x36), so the full word cannot receive one format name.
Independent VdSwap evidence names width and height from packed descriptor dword2, but no direct creator-to-descriptor correlation exists for these records; r4/r5 order remains numeric.
Static code proves a 0x34-byte creator result and builder path, while the accepted runtime probe emitted no header words or requested sizes; no per-set size or backing identity can be promoted.
The accepted alternate join reaches shared creator 0x82533DB8, but explicit-buffer vtable 0x8204767C and its +0x90/+0x94/+0x98 fields remain a separate wrapper type.

provider.resolveJoin: RVA-F-0140 proves that the first output of the runtime-selected provider reaches Resolve r6 unchanged. The observed vptr and slot identify 0x82517800, so the alternate Resolve resource is exactly the selected wrapper's +0x14 value.

wrapperLayout.extent: Factory 0x82517EC0 allocates 24 bytes. Constructor-style initialization installs vptr 0x82047628, initializes +0x04, +0x08, +0x0C, and +0x14 to zero, initializes +0x10 to 0x100, and then overwrites only the low 16 bits at +0x10 from the configuration input.

fields.0x04: Atomic wrapper reference count used by publication links.
fields.0x08: Pointer to the distinct publication link that retains this wrapper.
fields.0x0C: Pointer to an optional 68-byte copy of factory configuration metadata.
fields.0x10: Configuration halfword; no generation role is supported.
fields.0x14: Returned resource pointer exported by provider 0x82517800.

wrapperLayout.qualification: The 24-byte allocation proves this wrapper extent only. The 68-byte copied block is separate metadata and is not the returned resource header or backing.

creationAndPublication.factory: 0x82517EC0 allocates and initializes the 24-byte wrapper. It treats r4 as publication-head storage, r5 as source/context, and r6 as configuration input.
creationAndPublication.creatorInputs: Source/context virtual slots +0x48 and +0x4C produce two creator arguments. Helper 0x8251C9C0 produces a configuration pointer; its +0x0C word, after one bounded conditional patch, becomes another creator argument.

creatorInputMap.r4: First extent-like creator input from source/context virtual +0x48; ordered width versus height remains unresolved.
creatorInputMap.r5: Second extent-like creator input from source/context virtual +0x4C; ordered width versus height remains unresolved.
creatorInputMap.r6: Third creator input, observed as literal 1; depth/count-like role remains unresolved.
creatorInputMap.r7: Packed selector word from configuration +0x0C after its bounded conditional patch. The low six bits are a format field: accepted values 0x06 and 0x36 match Xenos k_8_8_8_8 and k_2_10_10_10_AS_16_16_16_16; upper bits remain numeric and unnamed.
creatorInputMap.r8: Fifth creator input, observed as literal 0; semantic role remains unresolved.
creatorInputMap.qualification: These are exact source positions and constants at the alternate factory pre-call boundary. Only the low-six-bit r7 format names are supported by accepted Xenos value-domain evidence; r4/r5 order, r6, r7 upper bits, and r8 retain qualified numeric roles.

creationAndPublication.dynamicCreator: At pre-call boundary 0x82517FFC the factory dispatches through the current device's vtable slot +0x08 with r4/r5 from the context virtuals, r6 literal one, r7 from configuration +0x0C after its bounded patch, and r8 literal zero. The accepted run joins this dispatch to creator 0x82533DB8 and records three input sets; a non-null result is stored at wrapper +0x14.

builderTrace.headerFacts: The creator result extent is exactly 0x34 bytes. The primary and optional secondary allocation requests and packed header words are not emitted by the accepted probe, so no exact per-set output sizes or header values are promoted.
builderTrace.basePatch: 0x826B7140 patches header +0x20 with the primary page base always and patches +0x30 with the secondary page base only when secondary backing exists; each preserves low 12 bits. This proves address publication adjustment, not backing identity or lower ownership.

The link is stored through the publication head and at wrapper +0x08, and link +0x10 points to the wrapper.

creationAndPublication.qualification: The accepted run joins one runtime wrapper/resource token to 0x82517EC0 and creator 0x82533DB8, with three input sets. Publication-head and outer-container ownership outside these exact edges remain unresolved.

headerAndBacking.result: The 0x34-byte creator result extent, builder chain, packed low-six-bit r7 format domain, and page-base adjustment are established. Exact per-set header words, primary or secondary requested sizes, lower allocation, backing storage identity, ordered dimensions, usage, allocation generation, and contents generation remain unresolved.

mutationAndReuse.resourceFieldWrites: Within the bounded wrapper closure, +0x14 is initialized to null, assigned the non-null dynamic creator result, read by the provider and bounded caller, used to locate the pointed resource's +0x04 reference count during release, and cleared. No static replacement setter is identified.
mutationAndReuse.configurationField: Wrapper +0x10 is a configuration halfword and is not an allocation or contents generation counter.
mutationAndReuse.linkReuse: An existing publication link may replace its retained wrapper target through 0x82347100. This is link-target reuse, not resource-memory or backing-address reuse.
mutationAndReuse.boundedNegative: No scalar generation, dirty publication, replacement, invalidation, allocation identity, contents identity, lower backing deallocation, or address-recycling policy is supported for the alternate resource. The accepted creator join adds no mutation, contents, lower-free, or recycling evidence. The same limits remain unresolved for the seven explicit-buffer candidate matches.

release.wrapperCleanup: 0x825180B8 loads wrapper +0x14 and atomically decrements the pointed resource's +0x04 reference count. When the count reaches zero it calls lower cleanup 0x82518B40, then clears wrapper +0x14. It passes wrapper +0x0C and size 68 to helper 0x82465DA8, then clears +0x0C.
release.linkCleanup: Link cleanup 0x823DC590 atomically decrements wrapper +0x04 and, when that count reaches zero, dispatches wrapper vtable slot +0x04. Its exact target 0x82359DD8 then tail-dispatches wrapper slot +0x00 with argument one. The link is passed to 0x82353A40, which installs a base vptr and decrements a global count; no link-storage deallocation is proved.
release.outerCleanup: The bounded outer container independently decrements its +0x58 resource's +0x04 and calls the same lower cleanup when that count reaches zero. No AddRef is visible at the wrapper +0x14 to outer +0x58 handoff.
release.lowerCleanup: 0x82518B40 classifies the resource dynamically and dispatches classifier code 3 to device slot +0x0C, code 17 to +0x1C, code 18 to +0x14, and code 19 to +0x24. Code 20 and other values take no lower release call in the bounded body.
release.qualification: The classifier and dynamic device calls do not identify a concrete lower destructor, backing deallocator, release completion point, or recycling policy. Reference decrements do not prove runtime destruction or address retirement.

entries.result: One exact pre-Resolve record selected vtable 0x82047628 and its +0x0C provider 0x82517800.
The provider exports wrapper +0x14 as its first output, zeroes its second output, and returns one.
The static factory, publication, reference-count, cleanup, and dynamic lower-release paths are bounded, and the accepted run joins one runtime wrapper/resource token to this factory and its creator.

The alternate factory pre-call supplies r4/r5 from source/context virtual +0x48/+0x4C results, r6 literal 1, r7 from configuration +0x0C after its bounded conditional patch, and r8 literal 0. Only r7 low-six-bit values 0x06 and 0x36 receive accepted Xenos format names; all other roles remain qualified.

Seven accepted matches join the alternate pre-call token to creator 0x82533DB8 and selected-slot-equals-r6; the three observed input sets are 0x400/0x400/1/0x18280106/0, 0x500/0x2D0/1/0x28280106/0, and 0x500/0x2D0/1/0x1A200136/0.

The matched creator allocates a 0x34-byte result, forwards extents and derived controls through the builder chain, and applies the page-base patch; exact per-set header words, requested sizes, and backing identity remain unobserved.

currentEvidence.qualification: Runtime evidence proves one selected vtable/provider identity, joins seven accepted input records to creator 0x82533DB8, and static evidence proves the provider output and builder chain. The run does not prove mutation, contents, lower allocation or free completion, backing release, or address recycling.

conclusion: One exact pre-Resolve runtime record selected vtable 0x82047628 and provider 0x82517800. That provider returns selected-wrapper field +0x14 as the first output that reaches Resolve r6, writes zero as its second output, and returns true. The accepted creator-input run joins the alternate factory pre-call 0x82517FFC to creator 0x82533DB8 for seven records and three sets: 0x400/0x400, 0x500/0x2D0 with r7 0x28280106, and 0x500/0x2D0 with r7 0x1A200136; r6 is one and r8 is zero in every set. The narrow static join proves r4/r5 are ordered extent-like inputs, r7 is a packed selector word whose low six bits are accepted Xenos formats 0x06 or 0x36, and the creator result is 0x34 bytes through the listed builder chain. r4/r5 order, r6 depth/count semantics, r7 upper bits, r8 semantic role, exact per-set header/size values, mutation or contents generation, lower allocation/free, and address recycling remain unresolved.
